documents.unit: Office of Academic Affairs & Provost (AI at Tulane site)
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence at Tulane University: Guidelines for the Ethical and Responsible Use of AI
documents.stance_why: The page sets no student rule of its own: it says student use is 'already covered in our academic integrity policies' and that 'Each instructor has the option of putting in place guidelines' for their course. Faculty are told 'Rather than restricting AI' to explore it. Decision handed to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: University AI page that frames AI as an opportunity and points student questions to existing integrity policies. It sets data-protection and security-review rules, leaves course rules to instructors with a clear-instructions requirement, and promises workshops and policy revision.

units.why: The opening states the university's purpose for AI: it 'recognizes the potential' of AI. This is a framing statement of principle, so P56 (institution-level framework/preamble), informs, general.
units.anchor: recognizes the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to reshape the educational and research landscape

units.why: States the guiding principle: reap AI's benefits 'while preserving the intellectual integrity and human-centered model'. A principle for the whole institution, so P56 rather than P87 (benefits only) since it balances benefit and integrity.
units.anchor: reap its benefits while preserving the intellectual integrity and human-centered model of our university

units.why: Describes investment in AI-related infrastructure for 'research, education management, operations and administration'. It covers AI in university operations beyond teaching, so P76 fits best; it is an institutional commitment, not a rule.
units.anchor: Investments in cross-disciplinary upgrades will support various university operations
units.fit_note: Describes infrastructure investment for operations rather than a rule governing operational AI use.

units.why: Cross-campus working groups are being formed 'to determine how AI can be applied across disciplines'. This describes the body and process creating guidance, so P84 (how and by whom the policy was made).
units.anchor: assembling experts in intellectual property, data privacy, and security

units.why: The provost 'established two committees' to learn about campus needs, which states who shaped the guidance, so P84; not P80 since the committees advise rather than enforce.
units.anchor: the provost established two committees to learn more about the current campus environment

units.why: Student AI use is governed by existing integrity policies rather than a new AI rule: 'already covered in our academic integrity policies'. This is P77 (follow existing university policy); P36 would need explicit mention of misconduct classification, which is absent here.
units.anchor: use of AI by our students are already covered in our academic integrity policies

units.why: Names concerns with AI ('accuracy, potential biases, and privacy'), an informing statement about harms. P53 fits bias; it also touches accuracy and privacy, so a fit note is added.
units.anchor: can raise concerns about accuracy, potential biases, and privacy
units.fit_note: Also names accuracy and privacy concerns, not only bias and ethics.

units.why: Users 'should consult with the necessary bodies' before using AI tools, a recommendation to check with authorities. P50 (prefer vetted tools, protect data) is nearest; no approved-tool list is named, so P65 does not fit.
units.anchor: students, faculty and staff should consult with the necessary bodies
units.fit_note: Asks users to consult review bodies before use; no specific approved tool list is named.

units.why: 'All members of Tulane University have a responsibility to protect university data', a duty binding everyone. P50 (protect personal and confidential data).
units.anchor: responsibility to protect university data from unauthorized access or disclosure

units.why: Data at Levels 2-4 'should not be entered into publicly available generative AI tools', a prohibition on inputs. P50 fits (protect confidential data); P20 is about assignment specs and student code, which this is not.
units.anchor: should not be entered into publicly available generative AI tools
units.policy: Data classified as Level 2-Internal, Level 3-Confidential Data or Level 4-Restricted should not be entered into publicly available generative AI tools.

units.why: Explains that prompts shared under default settings 'is not private', the reason for the data rule. P50 includes the fact that tools store prompts.
units.anchor: Information shared with generative AI tools using default settings is not private

units.why: 'must be applied to all technology solutions' sets a requirement for privacy and security considerations in tools. Best fits P65 (review of tools before deployment) in broadened form; it is general rather than AI-specific.
units.anchor: Appropriate privacy and security considerations must be applied to all technology solutions
units.fit_note: General requirement for all technology, not AI-specific.

units.why: Procured generative AI tools 'require a security and risk review' by a named office. This is review and approval of AI tools before deployment, P65, and also names who owns the review.
units.anchor: require a security and risk review by the Tulane Information Security Office

units.why: Directs users with questions about AI technology and data classification to the CISO. Naming a contact is closest to P80 (who owns the policy); P72 is about human help for learning, which is not this.
units.anchor: please contact ciso@tulane.edu
units.policy: Questions about AI technology, data classification levels or the review process go to ciso@tulane.edu.
units.fit_note: A help contact, not a statement of who enforces or grants exceptions.

units.why: 'faculty are encouraged to explore its potential' rather than restricting AI. This advises instructors to try AI before setting policy, P63 (support faculty in learning AI), and signals an encouraging stance.
units.anchor: Rather than restricting AI, faculty are encouraged to explore its potential
units.fit_note: Also sets a leaning against restriction, which P63 does not capture.

units.why: Explains why instructors should experiment: it identifies which projects AI handles well. Supports faculty learning, P63, informing.
units.anchor: Experimenting with AI can help identify which projects can be effectively handled

units.why: Suggests assignment designs ('incorporate personal experiences, cite sources accurately, or compare diverse ideas') that work in an AI context. These are assignment redesigns, P35.
units.anchor: requiring students to incorporate personal experiences, cite sources accurately, or compare diverse ideas

units.why: 'Everyone ... should actively engage' in AI integration, calling for community participation. P88 (engage peers, partners and the community on AI) is nearest; P66 is about instructors explaining to students.
units.anchor: should actively engage as we integrate AI into our educational and administrative processes
units.fit_note: Asks internal community members to engage, rather than external coalitions or forums.

units.why: 'Each instructor has the option' of setting course-specific guidelines: the decision is delegated to instructors, P04. The 'must be clear and precise' part is a separate clarity requirement (next unit).
units.anchor: Each instructor has the option of putting in place guidelines

units.why: Instructors 'must' make AI instructions 'clear and precise', a duty to communicate expectations. Closest to P09 (state expectations in syllabus or assignment) although no syllabus is named here.
units.anchor: instructions must be clear and precise
units.fit_note: Requires clarity of instructions but does not require a syllabus statement.

units.why: Where AI is permitted, students 'should be encouraged to describe how AI tools were used'. Disclosure with submission, P24, but only encouraged and not required.
units.anchor: students should be encouraged to describe how AI tools were used

units.why: 'on-going efforts to enhance and revise our policies' states the policy is provisional, P54.
units.anchor: on-going efforts to enhance and revise our policies

units.why: Instructors with questions about AI in teaching are sent to CELT, a faculty support channel, P63.
units.anchor: please contact celt@tulane.edu
units.policy: Instructors with questions about using AI tools in teaching or the classroom contact celt@tulane.edu.

units.why: The site is meant to keep the community informed about AI developments, which is P102 (stay informed) in spirit, though phrased as the university's service rather than a user duty.
units.anchor: established to share the latest advancements in AI advancements
units.fit_note: The university commits to publish updates; it does not tell users to stay informed.

units.why: The university will offer workshops 'to help the community understand and harness' AI. Training for the whole community, so P70 rather than P63 (faculty-only).
units.anchor: the university will introduce workshops to help the community understand and harness

documents.title: AI Research (Tulane student guidance on AI use)
documents.stance_why: The guide opens 'Tulane does not ban AI. Your instructor sets the rules for your course', and offers a cost-benefit ledger 'rather than a ban list'. No default allow or prohibit; the decision is delegated to the instructor, so delegates.
documents.summary: Library guide for students on using AI in research. It says Tulane does not ban AI, courses set the rules, and unauthorized generative AI breaches the Code of Academic Conduct, then sets out student duties to verify, disclose, protect data and weigh costs by research phase.

units.why: 'Tulane does not ban AI' states the default stance at the university level: no blanket ban. Coded as P02 rather than P04 because this sentence is about the absence of a prohibition; the delegation is the next unit.
units.anchor: Tulane does not ban AI.
units.fit_note: Says AI is not banned, not that it is welcomed.

units.why: 'Your instructor sets the rules for your course' delegates the decision to the instructor, P04.
units.anchor: Your instructor sets the rules for your course

units.why: Students are told to 'Check the AI statement in every syllabus, every semester'. A duty to find and follow each course's rules, P78 (P10 is ask when unsure; P09 is the instructor duty).
units.anchor: Check the AI statement in every syllabus, every semester.

units.why: 'academic integrity policies apply in full' says existing integrity rules continue to govern AI use, P77.
units.anchor: Tulane's academic integrity policies apply in full.

units.why: Defines AI: 'a broad term for computer systems that perform tasks usually requiring human intelligence'. A definition that sets scope, P61.
units.anchor: a broad term for computer systems that perform tasks usually requiring human intelligence

units.why: Defines generative AI by what it does ('Creates new text, images, summaries, or citations'), P61.
units.anchor: Creates new text, images, summaries, or citations by predicting likely patterns from training data.

units.why: Warns that generative output 'is not the same as accurate', P31 (AI output can be wrong).
units.anchor: Output is plausible-sounding, which is not the same as accurate.

units.why: Defines non-generative AI-assisted tools ('Searches, sorts, filters, and organizes'), scoping what the guide covers, P61.
units.anchor: Searches, sorts, filters, and organizes information that already exists, without inventing new content.

units.why: 'Vendors may log your searches' warns that tools retain user inputs, P50 (AI tools store prompts).
units.anchor: Vendors may log your searches.

units.why: 'sole author and intellectual owner ... fully responsible for any AI-generated content you incorporate' makes students own what they submit, P29.
units.anchor: You are the sole author and intellectual owner of your work

units.why: Unauthorized generative AI used 'to write or rewrite significant elements of your work' is 'a violation of the Code of Academic Conduct'. Two readings: P19 (no AI producing submitted work) and P36 (misconduct classification). P36 chosen because the sentence frames it as a Code violation and the ban depends on authorization.
units.anchor: using unauthorized assistance, including generative AI to write or rewrite significant elements of your work
units.policy: Using unauthorized assistance, including generative AI to write or rewrite significant elements of your work, is a violation of the Code of Academic Conduct.

units.why: States AI tools 'can invent sources, produce biased summaries, and make factual errors', P31 (AI output is often wrong).
units.anchor: AI tools can invent sources, produce biased summaries, and make factual errors.

units.why: Students are 'solely responsible for fact-checking and critically evaluating all AI-generated output', an explicit verification duty, P31.
units.anchor: solely responsible for fact-checking and critically evaluating all AI-generated output

units.why: 'Your grade rests on the accuracy of your submission, not the tool's' puts accountability for outputs on the student, P29.
units.anchor: Your grade rests on the accuracy of your submission, not the tool's.

units.why: Where AI is permitted students 'should describe how you used it', with an example statement. Disclosure with a submission, P24.
units.anchor: where AI use is permitted, you should describe how you used it

units.why: 'Failure to disclose ... may be treated as a violation' makes nondisclosure the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Failure to disclose when disclosure is expected is a breach of transparency

units.why: Same data rule as on the AI page, restated for students: Levels 2-4 data 'should not be entered into publicly available generative AI tools'. P50. Coded here because each document is coded on its own.
units.anchor: should not be entered into publicly available generative AI tools
units.policy: Data classified as Level 2-Internal, Level 3-Confidential, or Level 4-Restricted should not be entered into publicly available generative AI tools.

units.why: 'not private' with default settings explains the data rule, P50.
units.anchor: Information shared with generative AI using default settings is not private

units.why: Lists 'Energy and water consumed on every prompt' as a cost of generative AI in the cost-benefit ledger, an environmental concern, P53.
units.anchor: Energy and water consumed on every prompt

units.why: Students should 'weigh the gains against the costs' per task rather than default to use or avoidance. This is advice on judging when to use AI; no type matches a cost-benefit decision rule, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: weigh the gains against the costs for the task in front of you
units.uncovered_note: Students are told to weigh each AI tool's gains and costs for the research task at hand rather than follow a default.

units.why: Warns AI summaries do not build 'mental models and critical thinking skills that reading builds'; relying on AI undermines skill-building, P41.
units.anchor: Does not help build the mental models and critical thinking skills that reading builds

units.why: 'Reliance on AI summaries weakens synthesis capacity and critical evaluation' links reliance to lost skill, P41.
units.anchor: Reliance on AI summaries weakens synthesis capacity and critical evaluation

units.why: Warns uploading licensed content 'may violate terms', a licensing and data-retention concern, P52.
units.anchor: Uploading licensed content may violate terms and retain your data

units.why: Uploading library PDFs may 'violate university policies or publisher terms' and risk 'campus-wide access termination'. This concerns uploading course/library materials to AI, P49.
units.anchor: put the university at risk of campus-wide access termination

units.why: Directive 'Verify every citation against the actual source' for students who use generative tools, P31.
units.anchor: Verify every citation against the actual source; fabrication is common.

units.why: 'Assume your inputs may be used to train future models' warns about data reuse, P50.
units.anchor: Assume your inputs may be used to train future models.

units.why: Direct prohibition on pasting 'licensed, confidential, or unpublished content' into consumer AI tools; covers protected works, P49.
units.anchor: Do not paste licensed, confidential, or unpublished content into consumer AI tools.

units.why: 'Disclose your use to instructors, editors, or reviewers' requires disclosure of AI use, P24.
units.anchor: Disclose your use to instructors, editors, or reviewers.

units.why: Warns of 'intellectual gaps' from depending on AI; a skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: Account for the intellectual gaps that come from depending on AI-generated content.

units.why: Licensed content should be used 'only inside its native database's AI interface', a rule on which AI tools to use with library material, P92 (use approved tools).
units.anchor: use licensed library content only inside its native database's AI interface
units.fit_note: The approved environment is a vendor database's own AI, not a university-licensed tool.

units.why: States a limitation of AI tools ('cannot reach resources behind paywalls'). No type covers tool capability limits beyond wrong output; P31 is the closest.
units.anchor: AI cannot reach resources behind paywalls or subscription databases.
units.fit_note: Describes a capability limit rather than errors in output.

units.why: 'you must acknowledge it' makes acknowledgment of permitted AI use mandatory, P24.
units.anchor: If your instructor permits AI use, you must acknowledge it.

units.why: Students 'Consult your instructor for their preferred style' of AI citation, pointing to instructor discretion and asking, P10 (ask) with delegation.
units.anchor: Consult your instructor for their preferred style.
units.fit_note: Asks about citation style, not about whether use is allowed.

units.why: Distinguishes citation of specific output from a disclosure statement; 'most assignments that use AI need both'. P25 (cite the tool and output) fits because of the output-level citation; it also requires a general disclosure.
units.anchor: most assignments that use AI need both
units.fit_note: Also requires a separate disclosure statement about how AI was used.

notes: Coder A. Provost letter and Faculty Guide not available, so the default stance rests on the two collected documents. The cost-benefit table in the LibGuide was coded only where it made policy-like statements. The data-protection rule appears in both documents and is coded in each.
